Recommended architecture (concise)

- Use the Global Chart of Accounts master template as your starting point (under Global GL Defaults). Build your active company chart by selecting/assigning only the accounts you need from that master template; you may also create new accounts in the master if required, then assign them to organizations [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization.adoc-0][doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_AssignGlAccount.adoc-0].

- Model each physical store as an Organization (or department) within OFBiz. The Accounting model explicitly supports multiple organizations (companies, departments or other organizations) each having its own subset of GL accounts and reporting, so you can get per-store profitability and cash reconciliation while remaining one tax/legal entity overall [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/acc-intro.adoc-0][7766061-14].

- Typical per-store account assignments
  - Assign store-specific GL accounts (from the Global master) for: Cash/Bank, Sales/Revenue, COGS, Inventory, and any store-level receivables/payables so each store’s P&L and cash balances can be reported separately.
  - For central procurement and the central warehouse, use their own organization with its own assigned accounts.
  - For internal transfers between main warehouse and stores (and between stores), create/use inter-org transfer / inter-org payable & receivable accounts (defined in the Global master and assigned to the involved organizations) so transfers post and reconcile per store and central warehouse.

  (Create any of these accounts first in the Global master, then assign to the appropriate Organization) [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_AssignGlAccount.adoc-0][doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization.adoc-0].

- Journals and automated posting
  - Keep journal usage minimal; create organization-specific journals only if you need separate posting control per org. The system is designed to auto-create/post transactions from standard business events (sales, inventory transfers, invoices, payments) when GL defaults are mapped correctly [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/acc-intro.adoc-0].

- Important configuration note
  - If you create or replace standard accounts (e.g., Inventory) with your own custom accounts, you must update the GL defaults/configuration so all transaction types map to the correct accounts. Verify all references after changes. You can export chart details (CSV/PDF) for review [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization.adoc-0].

Suggested steps to implement
1. Review the Global master template and pick/rename accounts you’ll use for store-level Cash, Sales, COGS, Inventory, Inter-Org AR/AP, etc. [HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization].
2. Create any missing accounts in the Global master. [HELP_AssignGlAccount]
3. Create an Organization record for each store and for central procurement/warehouse; assign the appropriate subset of GL accounts to each Organization. [acc-intro][7766061-14]
4. Configure GL defaults so each business event (sales, receipts, inventory transfer) posts to the correct per-store and central accounts; test transfers and reconciliations. [HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization]

References: HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization, HELP_AssignGlAccount, acc-intro, Apache OFBiz Project Overview [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization.adoc-0][doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_AssignGlAccount.adoc-0][doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/acc-intro.adoc-0][7766061-14].

Short answer: the release workflow expects the release manager/PMC to publish CVE metadata and update the OFBiz security page (including links/references), and if that step wasn’t done the public security page will not show commit links. Also the project has relatively low commit/maintainer activity, which makes timely post-release housekeeping less reliable [48203381-7][63406655-6][42566016-0].

What you (or the release manager/PMC) can do
- Follow the Release Management Guide steps for CVE-bearing releases: complete the CVE information at the CVE process page, fill the 'vendor advisory' reference with your public announcement URL, update the security page on the site, update doap_OFBiz.rdf, and convert the related Jira into a security subtask (OFBIZ-1525) with a title starting “[SECURITY] (CVE-… )” [48203381-7].
- If you want to see commits in real time, subscribe to the commits mailing list (commits@ofbiz.apache.org) which notifies subscribers of repository commits [7766063-3].
- Note the project runs automated checks (CodeQL/OpenSSF/sonar/etc.) as part of CI; that helps find issues in code but does not replace the release-page bookkeeping described above [61330745-4].

If you want the project to add commit links for past CVE entries, ask the release manager/PMC to perform the Release Management Guide steps for those releases (complete CVE metadata and update the security page) so the links/refs will appear [48203381-7].

Short answer: You're not doing anything wrong with OFBiz — the problem is the demo data and default/demo permissions. The demo data ships with preloaded users/permissions that can let non‑admin demo accounts see/edit things (including changing UserLogin passwords), so your democustomer ended up able to edit the admin login. See docs below for evidence and recommended fixes.

Why this happens (docs):
- The tutorial shows the UI flow: if you can open a Party profile and click "Edit" in the User Name(s) form you can change a user password — i.e. the UI allows editing a UserLogin from the Party view [170266058-36].  
- The demo data includes an "admin" party and many predefined user logins and permissions; demo accounts and groups include many permissions by default [7045138-8] [7045140-1].  
- The Security Administration page warns that OFBiz is preloaded with user login IDs and security permissions that can act as "back doors" and must be secured before going online [48202125-1].  
- The production guidance is explicit: never use demo credentials in production (and change all demo passwords) [61330745-0] [7045138-8].

Recommended immediate fixes:
1. Treat this as insecure demo-data behavior — do not use demo users in production; change the admin password(s) now [61330745-0] [7045138-8].  
2. Inspect and remove any unwanted security groups/permissions from democustomer (or delete the democustomer account) so it cannot access Party/UserLogin edit screens [170266058-36] [7045140-1].  
3. For a proper deployment, create/load your own seed/ext data (or remove demo data) so no demo accounts/groups remain [7045138-8].  
4. Follow the OFBiz security hardening guidance to review Security*.xml, SecurityGroup and UserLoginSecurityGroup assignments and remove any unintended privileges [48202125-1].

If you want, tell me which security groups are assigned to democustomer (or paste the UserLoginSecurityGroup entries) and I can point to which permissions to remove based on the provided docs.

Short answer: this is expected when WebTools (Entity Engine + caches) tries to handle extremely large result sets in a JVM with insufficient heap and no server-side limiting. Fix by increasing the JVM heap (and initial heap), and by avoiding returning 20M rows in a single WebTools request — use pagination/streaming/summarization or a DB-side query that returns only the needed range. [7045138-31] [48201990-29] [430408379-16]

Actionable steps
1) Increase JVM heap and set a large initial heap
   - Raise -Xmx to a large fraction of server RAM (guide: around 75% of available memory) and raise -Xms so it is not tiny (make Xms fairly high or equal to Xmx to avoid cache thrashing). Example pattern shown: -Xms256M -Xmx2048M. Also ensure you run the OFBiz-required Java version. [7045138-31]

2) Avoid cache cannibalization (soft references)
   - Entity Engine caches use UtilCache with soft references. When the JVM needs more memory it runs GC and clears soft references; small Xms/Xmx makes caches get reclaimed repeatedly and causes GC overhead problems. Increasing heap and Xms reduces this behavior. [7045138-31] [48201990-29]

3) Don’t return huge raw result sets from WebTools — paginate/summarize or cap results
   - Tool/services that return large data sets should implement pagination, truncation or summarization at the service/tool boundary (ADR: configurable per-tool cap; default strategy is pagination/summarization/truncate). For 20M rows you must implement server-side pagination or an overflow strategy instead of trying to load everything into memory in WebTools. [430408379-16]

4) For database-intensive operations, tune the DB and architecture
   - For large searches focus on the database query performance and consider scaling (multiple nodes/load balancer) rather than pushing one instance to hold enormous result sets. [7045138-31]

If you want, tell me:
- current JVM args (-Xms/-Xmx) and available server RAM, and
- how you are invoking the find (WebTools view, custom service, or iterative paging),
and I’ll give specific heap values and suggestions for pagination/query changes.

Short recommendation — two supported integration patterns and the minimal OFBiz changes to make them work.

1) Choose how the React app will convey tenant context
- Domain-based (preferred when you can give each tenant a hostname): host the frontend on a tenant-specific domain (e.g. abc.com) so requests arrive already scoped to that tenant; OFBiz supports front-store multitenancy by tenant-specific domain names and multiple domains per tenant [49579254-2][49579254-1].
- Tenant-ID in login/requests (works when one shared domain): require the React app to include the tenant ID in the login form or in each API call so OFBiz can pick the right data instance [14814279-1][49579254-1].

2) How OFBiz will isolate tenant data
- OFBiz uses a separate database per tenant; the backend selects the tenant database based on the tenant ID or tenant-specific URL/domain (a default DB is still available) [14814279-1][49579254-1].
- Make tenant-specific configuration attributes where needed and map domains to tenants if using domain-based routing [49579254-1][49579254-2].

3) Required OFBiz configuration changes
- Add or edit tenant config in OFBIZ-HOME/framework/entity/data/<yourTenantConfig>.xml and make the corresponding changes in entityengine.xml and ofbiz-component.xml so OFBiz can route to the proper database per tenant [14814279-3].

4) Operational benefits and notes
- Multi-tenancy in OFBiz was added in rev 927271; its design avoids server restarts and lets tenants load/manage data without admin command-line installs — useful for scaling many tenant instances from one codebase [14814279-1].
- Use the front-store multitenancy feature if you want the React frontend to appear as separate tenant sites (domains) while the single OFBiz codebase serves them [49579254-2].

Suggested minimal implementation steps (React + OFBiz)
- Pick domain-based or tenant-ID approach.
- Implement tenant selection in the React app (hostname detection or tenant field included in authentication/API calls) [14814279-1][49579254-2].
- Configure OFBiz tenant DB entries and entity engine/component XMLs as above so requests route to the proper DB [14814279-3].
- Test login and data isolation per tenant (verify login by tenant ID or tenant domain selects the intended database) [14814279-1][49579254-1].

Citations: [14814279-1], [14814279-3], [49579254-1], [49579254-2].

Short answer — two supported approaches shown in the docs:

1) Inline JDBC: put your SSL options into the jdbc-uri and keep the inline-jdbc element. Example (based on the docs — replace the jdbc-uri with your SSL-enabled URI):
<inline-jdbc jdbc-driver="org.postgresql.Driver" jdbc-uri="jdbc:postgresql://127.0.0.1:5432/ofbiz" jdbc-username="ofbiz" jdbc-password="ofbiz" isolation-level="ReadCommitted" pool-minsize="2" pool-maxsize="250"/>

(Example inline-jdbc shown in the docs) [6553994-2] [71013152-11].

2) Avoid credentials in entityengine.xml: use a JNDI datasource so the DB username/password live in the application-server/container datasource, not in OFBiz. The docs show the jndi-jdbc form (commented example) — uncomment/configure it and point it at your container-managed datasource:
<jndi-jdbc jndi-server-name="default" jndi-name="java:comp/env/jdbc/localpostgres" isolation-level="ReadCommitted"/>

(The commented jndi-jdbc examples are in the docs) [71013152-11] [71013152-12].

Notes:
- Use approach (1) if you must keep OFBiz managing the connection (then add the PostgreSQL JDBC SSL options into the jdbc-uri).
- Use approach (2) if you want to avoid storing username/password in entityengine.xml (credentials handled by the container).

References: inline-jdbc and jndi-jdbc examples in entityengine.xml [6553994-2] [71013152-11] [71013152-12].

Short answer: this looks like a memory / cache / GC issue rather than an I/O saturation problem. OFBiz uses soft-referenced caches that get aggressively cleared when the JVM has to grow or reclaim heap, so a large product/image set can trigger long pauses at startup unless the JVM heap is sized appropriately [7045138-31].

Recommended actions
1) Increase and stabilize the JVM heap: set -Xms high (close to -Xmx) and raise -Xmx so the JVM does not repeatedly resize and trigger GC that clears soft-reference caches. The docs recommend sizing Xmx to around 75% of available memory and making Xms “pretty high, perhaps even as high as the max.” Example JVM options in the startup script: JAVA_VMOPTIONS="-Xms768M -Xmx1024M …" (adjust per your server RAM) [7045138-31] [6553871-9].

2) Edit your service/startup script to pass the VM args (VMARGS / JAVA_VMOPTIONS) used when launching OFBiz so the running JVM gets the new heap settings (the init scripts show where to set these) [6553871-9] [6553871-7].

3) Ensure the host has enough RAM/CPU for your catalog size. System guidance: with Java 17, a couple CPU cores and 2–4GB RAM are a minimum for development; production with many products/images will need more and you should size the heap accordingly [13271447-2] [7045138-31].

4) Monitor caches and GC while starting (WebTools shows Soft Reference cache behavior). If you see soft-reference cache thrashing, that confirms heap pressure and the need to increase Xms/Xmx [7045138-31].

5) If startup bottlenecks persist, plan performance tuning and scaling (multiple nodes / load balancing) and database tuning for product-heavy operations, as larger catalogs often require tuning beyond a single instance [7045138-31] [6553967-12].

References used: [7045138-31], [6553871-9], [6553871-7], [13271447-2], [6553967-12].

Short answer: Yes — that’s the recommended OFBiz pattern for a 3PL WMS, with two important caveats.

Why it works
- Using non-sales types prevents the auto-invoice / auto-payment ECAs from firing — billing is gated on SALES types, so a FULFILLMENT_ORDER / FULFIL_SHIPMENT will not trigger order-to-cash [430409055-3].

Must-dos / caveats
- Keep FULFILLMENT_ORDER truly standalone (do not make it a child of SALES_ORDER) or sales logic can re-attach via parent-type checks [430409055-2].  
- The built-in “one-call” shipping path is sales-coupled (quickShipEntireOrder and related helpers expect SALES_ORDER/SALES_SHIPMENT). You must drive lower-level services in sequence (receive → storeOrder/approve → reserve → pick → createShipment/createItemIssuance + createInventoryItemDetail → update shipment states → poll) and hand-roll the issuance path because OFBiz lacks a complete non-sales “issue inventory to shipment” service [430409055-4]. Set availableToPromiseDiff = 0 when creating item issuance so you don’t double-subtract ATP [430409055-4].  
- The auto-invoice on shipment is an ECA that has no config property to turn it off — hence the non-sales-type approach is necessary rather than trying to disable the ECA [430409055-1].

Tenancy / data model
- The suggested multi-merchant tenancy model (ProductStore per merchant, ProductStoreFacility to bind warehouse, InventoryItem.ownerPartyId to track merchant ownership, orders isolated by OrderHeader.productStoreId) is the documented approach and requires no new tables [430409055-5].

Conclusion
- Your setup (FULFILLMENT_ORDER + FULFIL_SHIPMENT; commingled stock with InventoryItem.ownerPartyId; ProductStore per merchant) is the documented/right approach for a 3PL in OFBiz — just implement the non-sales service flow and heed the ATP/issuance warning above [430409055-2][430409055-3][430409055-4][430409055-5][430409055-1].

Short answer — do two parallel imports and add a little custom wiring:

1) Inventory (register goods sold)
- Don’t try to use the one-call “sales shipment” flow without a Sales Order. OFBiz’s shipping/stock pipeline is sales-coupled and there is no complete non‑sales “issue inventory to shipment” service, so hand‑roll the issuance/stock change steps yourself: use createItemIssuance + createInventoryItemDetail to remove stock and set availableToPromiseDiff = 0 (take care not to subtract ATP twice). [430409055-4]

2) Financials (cash/card receipts / bank side)
- Represent the POS/merchant bank or cash account as a FinAccount and import the aggregated payment/batch data into that account. You will need a parser per input format and a common statement/line structure (statement id/date/lines, txn date/description/doc no/credit/debit, balances). Store lines, match or create corresponding accounting transactions, and mark lines as reconciled. OFBiz doesn’t yet provide an automatic bank‑statement → GL sync out of the box, so provide a matching UI and services to create the accounting entries that mirror the FinAccount transactions. [6553752-1] [6553752-0]

3) Glue / recommended flow for each POS batch
- Parse batch file → create bank/FinAccount statement lines.
- For inventory: call your custom service that does createItemIssuance + createInventoryItemDetail (ATP handling noted above) to decrement stock for sold items. [430409055-4]
- For payments: create the corresponding accounting/payment records linked to the FinAccount and/or invoices; match and reconcile the statement lines to those records via your UI/service so GL and FinAccount balances stay in sync. [6553752-1]

4) Use existing OFBiz capabilities where possible
- OFBiz includes a POS module and accounting features (invoices, payments, billing accounts) that you can reuse for per‑transaction handling; for aggregated/batched imports you’ll need the custom import/parsers and the issuance/accounting wiring described above. [6553827-1]

What to customize
- Parser(s) for your POS/processor/export format(s).
- Services/UI to: import statement/batch lines into a common structure, create/match accounting transactions, create item issuance records (createItemIssuance + createInventoryItemDetail), and reconcile FinAccount ↔ GL balances.

Short answer: Yes — OFBiz provides a REST plugin/component (rest-api) to expose services as REST endpoints out of the box. [doc:framework/rest-api/src/docs/asciidoc/rest-api.adoc-0][340037428-0]

How to enable/use it (concise):

- Dynamic exposure of existing services
  - Mark the service in its service definition with export="true". The service becomes available at /rest/services/{service_name} and accepts GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE. [340037428-2]
  - Parameter rules: for GET put a JSON object into the inParams query parameter; for POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE send a JSON object in the request body. Example:
    curl -k -X GET "https://localhost:8443/rest/services/findProductById?inParams=... " -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer <THE JWT>" [340037428-2]

- XML-defined REST APIs (recommended for custom resources)
  - Create a .rest.xml (following rest-api.xsd) in the api directory of your OFBiz component (e.g. framework/rest-api/api/exampleApiDefinition.rest.xml). Define <api>/<resource>/<operation verb="..."> entries mapping HTTP verbs (get, post, put, patch, delete) to OFBiz services. [340037428-4][doc:framework/rest-api/src/docs/asciidoc/rest-api.adoc-0]
  - Note: newer trunk features (customHeaders, primaryPermission, mainAction) exist but are not present in release24.09. [340037428-4]

- Swagger UI for the REST API docs is available at:
  https://localhost:8443/docs/swagger-ui.html [340037428-5]

Short answer: model "box" and "piece" as separate sellable products (or as configurable/variant options if you need one SKU/UI), and set the product price for each unit as "price per sqm × sqm per unit". That enforces integer quantities (whole boxes or whole pieces) in the cart.

Why and how (references from OFBiz docs)
- Products support features and multiple prices; product entities are where you attach descriptive data like dimensions and set prices per product/period [7766061-9].  
- OFBiz pricing is flexible (catalog manager sets base prices and price types/date ranges), so for each sellable unit (box or piece) you can set the correct price (65 × 1.44 for a box, 65 × 0.36 for a piece) as that product's price [73634382-10].  
- The ecommerce shopping list/cart allows updating item quantities (so customers/sellers can only change integer counts of the sellable product you expose) [158877148-58].  
- If you prefer a single product page with selectable options, OFBiz supports configurable products (demo PC001) where configuration options produce a configured product instance (and tie into manufacturing if needed) — this is a heavier-weight route if you need configuration logic rather than simple separate SKUs [6553921-0].

Recommendation
- Simpler: create two SKUs (Lorinzo-piece, Lorinzo-box). Record the dimensions as product features and set each SKU's price to the sqm price × area-per-unit. Expose both SKUs in the catalog so sellers pick the correct one and only enter integer quantities. References: [7766061-9], [73634382-10], [158877148-58].  
- If you need a single product page with option choices and automated creation of a configured SKU (and possible manufacturing steps), use the configurable product approach (demo PC001) — see [6553921-0] and [7766061-9].

Short answers:

1) Yes — async services use the Job Scheduler which runs a poller thread plus a pool of invoker threads; the pool is configured and therefore limits thread creation (not necessarily one thread per job) [48201960-3]. Invoker threads are bounded by the configured max-threads (and at least min-threads), and each invoker can run multiple jobs (the jobs attribute) before being destroyed — so 1,000 async runs will not necessarily create 1,000 threads; the number of concurrent threads will be limited by max-threads and other pool settings [48201960-3]. Also note services can be invoked in async mode via the service tag (mode="async") [50233686-9].

2) Yes — you can change the thread-pool settings. The thread-pool tag provides attributes you can set: min-threads, max-threads, jobs (max jobs per invoker thread), ttl, wait-millis, poll-enabled and poll-db-millis to control behavior and lifecycle of invoker/poller threads [48201960-3].

Most likely the tenant has not been granted the security/permission for your new component. When you create a component you must load its security data (that grants the admin user access) and restart/reload OFBiz so the new security entries are applied.

Steps to fix (from the docs)
- Ensure your component has the SecurityData XML in its data folder (e.g. hot-deploy/mycomponent/data/MyComponentSecurityData.xml) and that the base-permission is set when creating the component [14058653-8].  
- Load the security data into the running instance (this is what grants admin access). The tutorial shows using the install seed target: ./ant run-install-seed which loads MyComponentSecurityData.xml and grants access to admin [14058653-8].  
- Alternatively reload data / restart OFBiz after adding the component so security data is applied (./gradlew loadAll ofbiz is shown in the tutorial) and then browse to https://localhost:8443/<your-component> and login with admin/ofbiz [184617942-7][6553969-7].  
- If you used an older tutorial flow, also consider running the general install targets (run-install) and the create-admin-user-login target to populate DB users/permissions as needed [9012088-3].

If after loading the security data you still see "You cannot login to this application", re-check that the security XML actually contains the permission entries for the same base-permission/webapp name you created (so the admin user is actually granted that permission) and then reload as above [14058653-8][184617942-7].

1) Pagination repeating / showing all items — this is a known UI/pagination inconsistency. The UI docs note problems with the "navigation-form-name" / custom paginate-target approach (last button sometimes broken) and recommend using the standard/direct page-access pagination or make the navigation form work consistently. Also there are multiple reported pagination bugs (counts / pages mismatch) in various screens. Try removing custom navigation/paginate-target and use the standard pagination, or adjust your widget.form.defaultViewSize (the docs note problems when that is small) to see if the last/next buttons behave correctly [7766043-10] [46632560-0].

2) Renaming the list so the grid shows nothing — the grid/list widget expects the view to iterate a named list/variable. In the ZK example the grid/listbox uses the variable "persons" provided by the code and iterates it; likewise your grid's list-name must match the list name/result-map-list returned by the service. If you rename the list in the grid, make sure the service result-map-list (or the code variable the grid iterates) uses the same name, otherwise no records will be rendered [6553840-4].

If you want, paste the grid fragment + the service result-map/result-map-list and your paginate attributes and I can point out the exact mismatch to change.

Most likely the component is not linked/loaded for that tenant or its security wasn’t installed into the tenant DB. Check these things:

1) Confirm the component is connected to the tenant (TenantComponent). Multi-tenant uses Component and TenantComponent entities; you must add e.g. <TenantComponent tenantId="tn1" componentName="cpn1"/> so the component is known for that tenant [14814279-9].

2) Make sure the tenant config files are present and referenced in ofbiz-component.xml and loaded at the correct reader level. The tenant config must be loaded before OFBiz can address tenant datasources; pay attention to the reader order (seed / seed-initial / ext) when loading data [14814279-5][14814279-3].

3) Load the component/security into the tenant database (use the tenant delegator). Either use the multitenant install targets (ant run-install-multitenant / ant load-demo-multitenant) or run the java -jar -install commands specifying the delegator for each tenant (e.g. …-delegator=default#DEMO1) so the component’s seed/security data is installed into that tenant [14814279-9][14058653-8].

4) Ensure the component’s security data was installed (run-install-seed loads the component security in hot-deploy/<component>/data/... and grants admin access) and restart/reload OFBiz so menus/screens pick up the new component [14058653-8][6553969-7].

If you still can’t see it: verify the TenantComponent row exists for that tenant and that you used the correct delegator when installing the seed/security data.

Recommended architecture (concise)

1) Base on the Global Chart of Accounts master template
- Use the supplied Global GL Defaults as your master COA and pick/assign the accounts you will actually use for the company. Create any new accounts first in the Global COA, then assign them to the company chart [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization.adoc-0] [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_AssignGlAccount.adoc-0].

2) Tax/legal reporting = single Company organization; operational analysis using internal organizations
- Keep one Organization (Company) for tax/legal reporting (one tax entity). For profitability and cash tracking create internal Organisations (departments/warehouses/procurement centre) as organization entities inside OFBiz — the accounting model supports multiple organisations (they can represent departments or warehouses) and each org can have its own subset of the master COA and journals to track internal results separately [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/acc-intro.adoc-0] [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization.adoc-0].

3) GL-account defaults and mappings you should configure
- At minimum configure and check GL defaults for: Inventory, COGS, Purchases/AP, Sales/AR, Cash/Bank, and Inter-warehouse / transfer clearing accounts. If you create/replace any of the standard accounts (e.g. Inventory) you must update GL defaults to point to your custom account(s) so automatic posting works correctly [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization.adoc-0] [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_AssignGlAccount.adoc-0].

4) Centralized procurement and internal warehouse transfers
- Model centralized procurement as a single procurement organisation (or use the Company-level procurement GL accounts) so purchasing activity posts to the central purchase/AP accounts. Model each warehouse as an internal organisation (or as location-level sub-accounts) so internal stock transfers create inventory-transfer transactions that post to the configured inventory and transfer-clearing accounts. OFBiz favors automatic posting from business events (purchase/sales/inventory transfers/payments) rather than manual journal entries, so ensure your GL defaults and org assignments are correct for those event-driven postings [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/acc-intro.adoc-0] [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization.adoc-0].

5) Use journals minimally; use budgeting/reconciliation features for monitoring
- Minimize manual journals; rely on system posting from business documents. Use the budgeting and GL reconciliation features to reconcile profitability and cash by period and org/fiscal period summaries to support analysis and tax reporting [7766061-14] [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/acc-intro.adoc-0].

Quick implementation checklist
- Review Global GL Defaults and select accounts to use. Export CSV/PDF for review if helpful.  
- Create any new accounts in the Global COA, then assign them to the company chart.  
- Create internal Organisations for warehouses/departments (if you want separate P&L/cash tracking) and assign their GL accounts.  
- Configure GL defaults: Inventory, Transfer Clearing, Purchases/AP, Sales/AR, Cash/Bank, COGS, etc. Test purchase, sales, payment and inventory-transfer postings.  
(References: configuration/assignment and organization behavior above) [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization.adoc-0] [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_AssignGlAccount.adoc-0] [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/acc-intro.adoc-0] [7766061-14].

Yes — your design is the documented pattern.

Key points from the write‑up you followed

- Suppressing order‑to‑cash: use non‑sales order/shipment types. OFBiz’s billing ECAs are gated on sales types, so a non‑sales order/shipment simply won’t match the invoice/payment triggers (auto‑invoice fires for SALES_SHIPMENT, auto‑payment for SALES_ORDER). Result: no invoice, no payment, no accounting postings by construction [430409055-3].

- The trap to avoid: the out‑of‑the‑box quickShipEntireOrder/“one‑call” shipping path assumes SALES_ORDER/SALES_SHIPMENT and will cause invoice ECAs to run (there is no config property to turn that invoice ECA off). So don’t use the quick path for 3PL flows [430409055-1].

- What to do instead: drive the lower‑level services yourself in this order — Receive (receiveInventoryProduct), Intake (storeOrder as FULFILLMENT_ORDER + approve), Reserve (reserveStoreInventory), Pick (observe reservation), Track (createShipmentRouteSegment), Ship (createShipment → issue items → updateShipment states PACKED → SHIPPED), then Poll/report back. Also note OFBiz lacks a complete non‑sales “issue inventory to shipment” service: hand‑roll issuance with createItemIssuance + createInventoryItemDetail and set availableToPromiseDiff = 0 so ATP isn’t double‑decremented [430409055-4].

- Tenancy model (many merchants, one warehouse): everything uses stock entities (no new tables). Typical mapping:
  - Operator = PartyGroup; Warehouse = Facility (type WAREHOUSE) owned by operator
  - Merchant client = PartyGroup; merchant’s account = ProductStore (payToPartyId = merchant)
  - Warehouse→store link = ProductStoreFacility; API grant = ProductStoreRole (FULFILL_API_CLIENT)
  - Order isolation via OrderHeader.productStoreId; commingled inventory tracked by InventoryItem.ownerPartyId
  Onboarding a new client is just creating these data records — no code change [430409055-5].

Bottom line / recommendation
- Your approach (custom non‑sales OrderType + non‑sales shipment, avoid sales quick‑paths) is exactly the documented 3PL pattern. Be sure you implement the lower‑level flow and the item‑issuance workaround so shipments and ATP stay correct, and use the ProductStore / ownerPartyId mappings for tenancy [430409055-3][430409055-1][430409055-4][430409055-5].

1) Yes. The job scheduler that runs async/scheduled services uses a pool of invoker threads (plus a poller thread) and is configured with a thread-pool tag that controls behavior including the maximum number of invoker threads to create [48201960-3].

2) Yes. You can change the pool behavior/size via the thread-pool attributes (notably min-threads and max-threads); other configurable options include ttl, wait-millis, jobs, poll-enabled and poll-db-millis. Async services are submitted to the JobManager which uses this scheduler/thread pool [48201960-3][27826612-4].
